title: AI Builders Digest
subtitle: Bilingual edition · 双语对照版

intro.text: 今天的主线不是某个新模型，而是 AI 正在重新安排产品、工作流和安全边界：人们开始为 agent 设计产品，builder 则用每天动手来理解模型、工具和 harness。与此同时，agent 一旦能替人完成端到端任务，权限、交易和基础设施就不再是后台细节，而会变成产品本身。

archive.title: Agent 重排日报
archive.desc: 个人 agent 正从聊天工具变成能完成任务的执行层，产品入口、builder 学习方式与安全防线都随之重排。

footerNote: Source: Follow Builders curated daily digest. Rebuilt from the 2026-09-20 source feeds.

sections.title: Agents Become the New User / Agent 成为新用户
sections.desc: 当 agent 可以替用户完成一整段流程，产品需要争取的注意力就不只来自人，也来自能否被 agent 调用。

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie argues that personal agents turn ‘build something users want’ into ‘build something agents want.’ A useful product must let an agent take a task, navigate tools or a CLI, transact, and finish the job end to end. That changes the competitive surface of consumer software: the winners may be the services easiest for agents to order from, book through, and connect to.
original: Personal agents are the ultimate manifestation of “build something that agents want”.
The new attention you need to compete for is not from the user itself but instead for the agent.

rewrite: Box CEO Aaron Levie 认为，personal agent 把「做用户想要的东西」改写成了「做 agent 想要的东西」。产品必须让 agent 接手任务、操作工具或 CLI、完成交易，并把整件事端到端做完。未来被更多使用的，可能是最容易让 agent 下单、订票、接入数据的服务。
original: Personal agents are the ultimate manifestation of “build something that agents want”.
新的竞争注意力不再只来自用户本身，而是来自 agent。

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch sees the most important effect of the current AI wave in the people building with it. Beneath the short-term drama, more people are choosing to create and ship instead of only consume. The technology matters because it widens the set of people who can turn an idea into something real.
original: The coolest thing about the recent wave of AI is that everyone is excited about building.
The people want to create and ship, not just consume.

rewrite: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 看到这轮 AI 浪潮最重要的影响：越来越多人开始用它来 build。撇开短期争议，人们正在从只消费内容，转向真正创造和发布东西。技术的价值在于，它扩大了能把想法变成现实的人群。
original: 最近这波 AI 最酷的地方，是每个人都对 building 感到兴奋。
人们想要创造和发布，而不只是消费。

sections.title: Learning by Tinkering / 动手才是理解方式
sections.desc: AI 变化太快，旁观者很难只靠听别人讲来跟上；持续做小项目，正在成为 builder 和投资人共同的学习方法。

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari explains why he spends about two hours a day programming despite being a VC: reading papers shows where models may improve, but building reveals which tools and harnesses let them complete long-horizon work. His practical advice is to tinker daily for ten days, replacing second-hand opinions with direct contact.
original: I spend ~2 hours a day programming, building side projects, tinkering obsessively, trying new repos..
You need to see what tools do they need to be successful and complete even longer long horizon tasks (infra)
Once you do it for 10 days, I’m sure you’ll be equally obsessed!

rewrite: Nikunj Kothari 解释了自己身为 VC 还每天写代码的原因：读论文能判断模型能力会往哪里走，但亲手 build 才能看见哪些工具和 harness 真能让模型完成长链路任务。他的建议很实际：连续十天每天动手，用一手体验替代二手判断。
original: 我每天花约两小时写代码、做 side project、沉迷 tinkering、尝试新 repo。
你需要看它们需要什么工具来完成更长的 long horizon 任务（infra）。
坚持十天，你也会同样上头。

rewrite: Peter Yang describes a small personal agent: a Markdown file records his ratings for movies, TV, and books, while a /tastemaker skill checks new releases and recommends things he has not seen. The interesting part is the pattern: a lightweight personal database plus a repeatable skill becomes more relevant as context accumulates.
original: I have a simple markdown file and a /tastemaker skill that I use to add ratings for movies, TV shows, and books I've seen.
Then every week it looks up new releases and stuff I haven't seen and makes incredibly relevant suggestions.

rewrite: Peter Yang 分享了一个很小、但很有代表性的 personal agent：用 Markdown 记录看过的电影、剧集和书，再用 /tastemaker skill 每周查找新作品，生成相关推荐。有意思的不是清单，而是一份个人数据库加一个可重复运行的 skill，随着上下文积累会越来越懂你。
original: 我有一个简单的 Markdown 文件和一个 /tastemaker skill，用来给看过的电影、剧集和书打分。
然后它每周查找新发布的内容和我没看过的东西，给出非常相关的推荐。

sections.title: The Security Cost of Agency / Agent 的安全代价
sections.desc: agent 从回答问题走向操作系统、网站和交易系统后，权限边界就必须和能力一起升级。

rewrite: Aditya Agarwal makes an alarming inference from recent announcements about agent intrusions by Gemini, OpenAI, and Anthropic: he takes it for granted that nation states have already penetrated some major companies without those companies knowing. This is a warning rather than a report of a specific breach, but it highlights how agent access can turn security failures into silent operational risks.
original: After seeing the rush of announcements by Gemini (Google), OpenAi and Anthropic about even more agent intrusions......I take it for 100% granted that a number of of major companies have been penetrated by nation states without them knowing about it.

rewrite: Aditya Agarwal 根据 Gemini、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 最近关于 agent intrusion 的公告，做了一个不安的推断：一些大公司很可能已经被民族国家渗透，只是自己还不知道。这不是对具体入侵的报道，而是一种警告：agent 一旦能跨内部工具执行操作，安全问题可能变成安静发生的运营风险。
original: 看到 Gemini（Google）、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 关于更多 agent intrusion 的一连串公告后，我百分之百确信，一些大公司已经被民族国家渗透，只是它们自己还不知道。

rewrite: OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux offers a compact prediction: 2026 is the year of the Linux desktop. In the context of this feed's agent focus, the line points toward a world where local environments and open tooling matter more as software agents become active participants in the workflow.
original: 2026 is the year of linux desktop

rewrite: OpenAI 的 Thibault Sottiaux 给出一个极简预测：2026 年属于 Linux desktop。放在 agent 逐渐进入工作流的背景里看，这句话指向一种可能性：当软件 agent 变成主动参与者，本地环境和开放工具的重要性会重新上升。
original: 2026 年是 Linux desktop 之年。

sections.title: From Language to Discovery / 从语言模型到科学发现
sections.desc: 今天唯一的播客把视线拉到更远处：AI 的下一步不只是更会聊天，而是把分散的知识、模拟和实验重新连接起来。

cards.authorTag: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck

rewrite: The takeaway: AI may become a bridge between fragmented scientific knowledge, simulation, and real-world experiments. Richard Socher argues that science has moved from a body of knowledge to a labyrinth of specialized fields, making cross-disciplinary insight increasingly difficult for humans alone. His proposed system combines knowledge, measurements, simulations, and experiments, with agents exploring hypotheses in parallel. The constraint is compute. The memorable claim is: ‘Anything you can simulate, AI will solve.’
original: Anything you can simulate, AI will solve. And before you know it, you're in this recursive self improvement loop and we believe that that will be a great unlock.
We evolved from a body of knowledge to a labyrinth of knowledge, 34,000 journals that might as well have no trespassing signs.
Compute is the biggest constraint.

rewrite: 核心 takeaway：AI 可能成为连接碎片化科学知识、模拟和现实实验的桥梁。Richard Socher 认为，科学已经从一套知识变成专业化迷宫，单靠人类越来越难完成跨学科连接。他的答案是把知识、科学测量、simulation 和真实实验放进同一个系统，让 agents 并行探索假设。真正的约束是 compute，最值得记住的一句话是：「任何能被 simulation 的东西，AI 都会解决。」
original: 任何能被 simulation 的东西，AI 都会解决。然后你很快就会进入 recursive self improvement loop，我们相信这会带来巨大的突破。
我们已经从一套知识走进知识迷宫，34,000 本期刊几乎都挂着禁止入内的牌子。
Compute 是最大的约束。
